idea-plugin.name: Codebook
idea-plugin.description:
Turns the prose in your comments into a readable book: a clickable topic outline, layered follow-caret notes with Markdown rendering, and Run/Debug buttons - while the comments themselves fold away in the editor, so the code stays readable and the explanation stays available.

A topic is a block comment whose first line is a dash-framed title - ---- topic ----, --- child ---, -- detail --, - aside - for the four levels. Markers are ordinary comments: they never break compilation and degrade gracefully in editors that know nothing about them. Supports block references and embeds between annotations ([text](#topic), ![](#topic)), cross-file references into other snippets or a Markdown glossary (dictionary.md#term - headings are the blocks there), output-section linking from source to the Run console, and per-course configuration via cbl.properties. Works in any JetBrains IDE - the parser is PSI-comment based and language-agnostic (C++, Python, Java, Kotlin, ...).

Built for the code-based-learning courses at codebasedlearning.dev.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Initial release
  • Topic outline of a file's dash-framed block comments, with layered notes that follow the caret.
  • Markdown rendering (GitHub-flavoured, tables included), images, and links between topics.
  • Short glossary references: [#term] links and ![#term] embeds, resolved along a configurable search path.
  • Editor folding of the note body, leaving the title line visible; fold and unfold act on the topic comments only.
  • Run and Debug from the panel; gutter icons link printed output sections back to their source line.
  • Per-course configuration via cascading cbl.properties.
